cues.text: A Dutch student who joined the newly founded Society of Jesus in its earliest years, Peter Canisius became, almost single-handedly, the public face of the Catholic response to the Reformation across the German-speaking lands.

He walked or rode an estimated twenty thousand miles over thirty years, preaching, founding colleges, and writing a catechism so clear and so widely translated that it shaped Catholic religious instruction for centuries after his death.

He represented the Church's interests at the Council of Trent and at difficult public conferences with Protestant theologians, always preferring, by his own account, to explain the faith's abiding truth rather than simply denounce his opponents' errors.
He spent his final, stroke-weakened years at Fribourg, Switzerland, where he is remembered as the second Apostle of Germany and, since 1925, as a Doctor of the Church.
